headline: GOLD ENDS WILD WEEK AT $4,178 AFTER CPI CRASH TO $4,098 — SILVER SWINGS 5.3% BEFORE FRIDAY REBOUND
snippet: Gold ended the week of October 12-17 at $4,177.82, down just 0.5% despite a violent midweek drop to $4,098.80 on October 14 after US September CPI came in at 0.6% month-over-month, briefly pushing Fed rate hike odds for the October 27-28 meeting toward 70%. Silver experienced a far more dramatic swing — plunging 5.3% from above $60 at its worst — before staging a 3.3% Friday rebound to close near $57.31/oz, with the gold/silver ratio ending near 72.8. What rescued both metals was a combination of Friday comments from Fed Chair Warsh at the IMF signaling no October rate hike, a 10-year Treasury yield falling to 5.08% as AI-linked tech stocks sold off sharply, and hike odds retreating to 29% by Friday's close. For retail investors in junior miners, this price arc confirms $4,100 as a strong support zone for gold heading into the October 27-28 FOMC meeting — but underlines that silver, now 54% below its 2026 high near $121/oz, remains a high-beta, high-volatility instrument where institutional unwinds can hit without warning.

headline: FED CHAIR WARSH SIGNALS OCTOBER RATE HOLD AT IMF — GOLD FIRMS NEAR $4,170 AS HIKE ODDS COLLAPSE FROM 70% TO 29%
snippet: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at IMF meetings on October 17 and offered no indication of a rate hike at the October 27-28 policy meeting — a significant dovish pivot from the 70% hike probability that had prevailed after Tuesday's hot CPI reading. Spot gold responded by trading near $4,170-$4,185 on Friday, recovering from an intraday low of $4,098 struck on October 14. The October 27-28 FOMC meeting is now positioned as the single most important near-term catalyst for gold and junior mining equities — a hold is now priced at roughly 71% probability, but any hawkish surprise could retest $4,100 support and simultaneously reprice junior developer financing assumptions. The episode also puts Warsh's credibility on Fed independence in focus: markets have learned to treat his IMF and conference remarks as policy signals, not academic commentary, making every public appearance a potential volatility event for precious metals. For TSX-V and ASX junior miners, the dovish signal maintains the financial conditions environment that supports equity risk appetites heading into a critical Q4 earnings and resource update season.

headline: SILVER SPLITS FROM GOLD DURING AI TECH ROUT — COREWEAVE-LED SELLOFF LIFTS GOLD 1% BUT SILVER HITS 3-MONTH LOW
snippet: On October 15, a CoreWeave-led AI and technology stock selloff drove global equities lower and pushed 10-year Treasury yields to three-week lows at 5.08%, fuelling haven demand that lifted gold roughly 1% to $4,147.50. Silver, however, failed to participate and hit a three-month low — a striking divergence that BullionVault attributes to silver's higher sensitivity to industrial demand prospects being repriced as AI investment efficiency concerns emerge. The gold/silver ratio above 72 marks the widest divergence since early 2026. For junior mining investors choosing between gold-focused and silver-focused exploration companies, the divergence is a data point worth tracking: gold's monetary haven premium is currently supporting valuations even in risk-off tech-driven episodes, while silver's industrial demand assumptions (tied to solar manufacturing and EVs) are being questioned. Historically, gold/silver ratio extremes above 70-75 have preceded significant silver catch-up moves — the same ratio that signals short-term weakness in silver often marks the setup for a longer-term re-rating.

headline: GOLD'S WORST WEEK OF 2026: CENTRAL BANKS FILED A RECORD BUY SIGNAL WHILE RETAIL SOLD — SOVEREIGN FLOOR HOLDS
snippet: GoldSilver.com's analysis of gold's worst weekly drawdown in 2026 highlights a striking counter-trend: even as institutional and retail investors reduced gold exposure during the correction, central banks purchased a record 289 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026 — a 62% year-over-year increase and the highest second quarter on record — buying continued even as gold prices fell 14% during that quarter. Poland led sovereign buying with 51 metric tonnes added, and China purchased 33 metric tonnes in Q2, its largest quarterly addition since late 2023; Russia sold 22 tonnes. The analysis frames this as a fundamental divergence between short-term paper-market selling and long-term strategic physical accumulation, arguing that sovereign demand provides a structural price floor that periodic macro-driven corrections cannot permanently pierce. For retail mining investors, the central bank buying trend represents a durable fundamental support for gold price assumptions underlying junior explorer valuations — even as the gold equity sector has corrected 35-40% from 2026 cycle highs on rising real yields and cost inflation concerns.

headline: TECTONIC METALS DRILLS 2.41 G/T AU OVER 59M AT ALASKA'S ALPHA BOWL — 29,000M SEASON, CORRIDOR AT 300M DEPTH
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSX-V: TECT) released assay results from 19 drill holes at its Flat Gold Project in southwest Alaska on October 15, with the headline hit from Alpha Bowl returning 2.41 g/t gold over 59.44 metres (hole CMR26-170), including 11.82 g/t over 10.67 metres and a higher-grade section of 39.96 g/t over 3.05 metres. At the Adit Zone, hole CMR26-163 returned 1.52 g/t over 42.67 metres, with a 27.35 g/t bonanza section inside. The company has now drilled over 29,000 metres at Flat Gold in 2026 and confirmed the Chicken Mountain higher-grade corridor to a 300-metre vertical depth across a 3.3 kilometre strike length. Drilling continues through the end of October. For junior mining investors evaluating Alaskan gold assets, Flat Gold stands out for its combination of broad mineralized intervals, multiple targets generating consistent results, and an established 3+ km footprint that de-risks the scale thesis. All reported intervals are downhole widths; true widths are not yet confirmed and should be considered when evaluating the intercept economics.

headline: ANTOFAGASTA Q3 COPPER MISSES AT 151,900T — SHARES FALL 7% AS 9-MONTH OUTPUT DROPS 8% AND 2027 GUIDANCE SOFT
snippet: Antofagasta (LSE: ANTO) reported October 15 that Q3 2026 copper production rose 7% quarter-on-quarter to 151,900 tonnes as Los Pelambres recovered from July weather disruption — but the result came in below Peel Hunt's 158,000 tonne estimate and shares fell as much as 7%. Nine-month 2026 output is down approximately 8% year-on-year at 436,900 tonnes, with weaker grades and recoveries at Centinela (still on strike) as the main drag. The 2026 guidance of 625,000-655,000 tonnes was maintained, but 2027 guidance of 630,000-690,000 tonnes came in below one broker's 710,000 tonne estimate. All-in cash costs were revised upward to $2.60-$2.70/lb for 2026, citing diesel prices. Antofagasta is the world's fifth-largest copper producer — when its largest mines keep missing quarterly estimates and cost guidance inflates, the implications are significant for global refined copper balances. For junior copper explorers, the result is a continued validation of the structural demand-supply thesis: Chilean production continues to disappoint relative to consensus expectations, making new mine supply from non-Chilean jurisdictions increasingly strategically valuable.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM ACQUIRES 55,000-HECTARE LOS ALTARES IN ARGENTINA'S CERRO SOLO URANIUM DISTRICT
snippet: Myriad Uranium (TSX-V / CSE: MYRD) announced October 13 that it has agreed to acquire the Los Altares uranium project in Chubut province, Argentina from Green Shift Commodities for $300,000 cash plus approximately 1.57 million shares — a total deal value well below $1 million for a 55,013 hectare, 23-property land position in the Cerro Solo uranium district, adjacent to CNEA's Cerro Solo deposit and UrAmerica's Meseta Central deposit. Four properties carry granted mining concessions with approved environmental impact assessments; the 2% NSR (with half repurchasable for $1 million) is standard structuring for an early-stage asset. The deal closes on or before November 13, subject to TSX-V and CSE regulatory approval. With uranium long-term contract prices at $96-97/lb — an 18-year high — and Argentina's Milei government actively courting mining investment with regulatory reforms, adding district-scale land in a historically significant uranium corridor for under $1 million represents the type of low-cost optionality building that characterises well-run junior uranium explorers. Note: the Qualified Person has not independently verified historical drilling data for Los Altares.

headline: ALKANE RESOURCES' 1,651M HOLE AT PEAK HILL FINDS EPITHERMAL ZONE 1KM DEEP — PORPHYRY TARGET LIES EVEN DEEPER
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK) reported October 14-15 that diamond hole PHD084 at its Peak Hill project in New South Wales — drilled to 1,651 metres — intersected transitional phyllic alteration and epithermal-style gold-copper mineralization approximately 1 kilometre below the Great Eastern open cut, but did not reach the sought-after porphyry intrusive target. The main intercept was 6.4 metres at 0.42 g/t gold from approximately 1,000 metres depth, with a lower-grade 153-metre interval at 0.11 g/t from 1,427 metres. A geological study has been commissioned to model the geometry of possible porphyry intrusives before further deep drilling; follow-up holes are planned for November. Alkane separately received an A$165,000 NSW Critical Minerals grant toward the program. For ASX junior mining investors, PHD084 confirms that a large, thermally active geological system sits beneath Peak Hill — a known gold-producing region — and that the porphyry target is a matter of depth and geometry, not existence. Alkane's funded exploration platform (underpinned by Tomingley gold production) allows it to persist in the deep hunt that many junior explorers could not afford.

headline: COPPER SUPPLY DEFICIT DEEPENS DESPITE PRICE PULLBACK — LME STOCKS FALL 1,625T, UBS MODELS 520,000T SHORTFALL
snippet: The International Copper Association Australia's weekly brief for October 15 shows outside-US LME copper stocks fell another 1,625 tonnes to 232,275 tonnes — with visible inventories outside the United States at multi-year lows — even as COMEX warehouse stocks inside the US sit at a record 711,609 tonnes, creating a bifurcated global market. Chilean first-half output is down approximately 6.6% year-on-year amid ongoing strike disruptions (Centinela remains on strike) and weather events; Morgan Stanley's deficit estimate reaches 600,000 tonnes if Chilean recovery does not materialise in H2, while UBS models 520,000 tonnes. For junior copper explorers on the TSX-V and ASX, the take-away is that the structural case for new mine supply is strengthening by the quarter: the gap between consensus demand growth of 2.8% and supply growth of 1.7% compounds every year, and the pipeline of Chilean projects facing permitting, community and technical delays is not closing that gap fast enough. Near-term price volatility driven by US CPI data and Fed rate hike fears does not change the structural supply story underpinning development-stage project valuations.

headline: BRIXTON METALS SAMPLES 195 G/T GOLD IN NEW GOLDEN VALLEY VEIN AT BC'S THORN PROJECT — DRILL TARGET FOR 2027
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSX-V: BBB) announced October 14 the discovery of a new high-grade gold-copper-silver vein at the Golden Valley target within its Thorn project in northwest British Columbia — located 17 kilometres southeast of its Trapper Gold target and 24 kilometres northwest of the past-producing Golden Bear gold mine. Four rock grab samples from the Golden Valley Vein returned between 17.9 and 195 g/t gold; the best grab reported 195 g/t gold, 147 g/t silver and 4.11% copper. Additional samples taken 400 metres south of the main outcrop returned 23.0 g/t gold, 58.7 g/t silver and 0.54% copper, with the vein exposing a 90-metre surface expression before disappearing under cover. Grab samples are selective and not representative of continuous mineralisation; however, multi-element bonanza-grade values at a new target within a large, multi-zone BC porphyry project are the type of discovery that earns prioritised follow-up in the next drill program. Thorn is a large, underexplored northwest BC property with multiple target types; Golden Valley expands the project's option set ahead of the 2027 field season.
